hero.headline: TCCEED doubles employer participation in second year of paid summer internship program
hero.body:
TCCEED placed 61 Treasure Coast students in paid summer internships this year as the second-year initiative doubled employer participation. The program saw applications from Treasure Coast students triple compared to the first year.

The expansion marks significant growth for the workforce development initiative connecting local students with paid work experience. Employers from across the Treasure Coast participated in the program.

The internship program provides students with hands-on job experience while earning wages during the summer months. TCCEED coordinates placements between participating employers and eligible students from the region.

The initiative runs through the summer season, with students completing their internships at local businesses and organizations throughout Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties.

cards.headline: Woman accused of using vehicle as weapon in St. Lucie County assault
cards.body:
Tioniea Hines, 22, sits in St. Lucie County Jail on $75,000 bond after being arrested on charges of using her vehicle as weapon in St. Lucie County assault

Tioniea Hines, 22, sits in St. Lucie County Jail on $75,000 bond after being arrested on charges of using her vehicle as a weapon against three people. She faces three counts of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon.

The arrest occurred Saturday in St. Lucie County. Authorities charged Hines after the alleged assault involving her vehicle and three victims.

Hines remains in custody at St. Lucie County Jail. The bond was set at $75,000 for the three counts of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon.

The three counts of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon indicate prosecutors believe Hines used her vehicle to intentionally harm three separate individuals. Each count represents charges for one of the three alleged victims in the incident.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Three-Game Skid With 4-1 Win Over Jupiter
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed o
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed only minutes to take control. The first three batters of the game all reached and scored before an out was recorded. Elian Peña opened with a single, Mike Tauchman doubled him home, and Trey Snyder followed with a two-run homer off Walin Castillo for a 3-0 lead.

Julio Zayas added a solo shot with two outs in the third to push the margin to 4-0.

That was more than enough for starter Emilio Obispo, who threw five shutout innings and lowered his season ERA to 1.82. He scattered four singles, walked three and struck out six to earn his fourth win of the year.

Obispo worked out of trouble when it mattered. He struck out Josh Hogue to strand the bases loaded in the third, induced a double play to end the fourth, and retired the side in order in the fifth to finish his outing.

Jupiter loaded the bases against Calvin Ziegler in the sixth. Ziegler struck out Jake McCutheon for the second out before Zack Mack entered and ended the threat with a popout. Mack went 2.1 innings and allowed one unearned run, which came in the eighth when Andres Valor stole third and scored on a throwing error.

Elwis Mijares closed it out with a 1-2-3 ninth on 11 pitches for his second save.

Tauchman, rehabbing a torn meniscus, went 1 for 3 with the double, an RBI and a run while playing six innings in left field in his first rehab game with St. Lucie. Snyder led the offense at 2 for 4 with the homer and two RBI.

The Mets (5-13, 38-46) and Hammerheads (8-12, 45-41) close their six-game series Sunday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. A win would give St. Lucie its first 3-3 series split of 2026. First pitch is 12:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Florida Homeowner Faces Uninsured Hurricane Milton Damage Two Months After Paying Off House
cards.teaser: A Florida resident who recently paid off his mortgage saw Hurricane Milton tear the roof from his home, leaving him to cover repair costs without insurance protection.
cards.body:
A Florida man completed paying off his house only to face major damage from Hurricane Milton two months later. The storm tore off his roof, creating extensive damage to the property he had just finished purchasing outright.

The homeowner was left without insurance coverage when the hurricane struck, forcing him to pay for all repairs from his own funds. Hurricane Milton caused the roof damage that left the recently mortgage-free property requiring significant reconstruction work. The situation highlights the risks Florida homeowners face when going without insurance coverage in a state prone to severe weather events.

cards.headline: TCCEED places 61 Treasure Coast students in paid summer internships, applications triple
cards.teaser: TCCEED expanded its paid summer internship program in its second year, doubling employer participation and placing 61 students in local jobs.
cards.body:
The second-year initiative saw applications from Treasure Coast students triple compared to the first year. Employer participation doubled, allowing the program to place 61 students in paid internships across the Treasure Coast.

TCCEED connects local students with businesses throughout Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties. The program provides students with work experience while helping local employers develop future talent.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie soccer stadium groundbreaking set for November, new renderings released
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie SC released new renderings of its 6,000-seat stadium at the Walton & One development on U.S. 1 and Walton Road, with groundbreaking planned for November.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie SC released new renderings this week of its 6,000-seat soccer stadium and announced Friday that groundbreaking is anticipated later this year, with current plans targeting November. The stadium will be built at the Walton & One development, a 46-acre mixed-use redevelopment project located along U.S. 1 and Walton Road. While the club's inaugural season begins in 2027, the future stadium is scheduled to open in early 2028. The team has not announced where they plan to play next year while the facility is under construction. The club posted Thursday on social media that their home venue will be a place where soccer, community, and unforgettable moments will come together. Calling it a year-round gathering place, the club said the venue will have the flexibility to grow in capacity.

Port St. Lucie resident Zach Woods said he thinks there is nothing to do in PSL for the most part and this may be the first cool thing the city has ever actually brought. Focus Sanders, a barber at Sapp's Barbershop, said it offers more business because it will bring more people to the area, including people coming from maybe out of town who didn't get a haircut. Woods said you can't really even get out on U.S. 1 before this and it's a nightmare, so he thinks the additional traffic on gamedays will be huge. Sanders said he is not liking the traffic that is going to come, but is liking the business traffic. The city was awarded a United Soccer League League One Team last October. Port St. Lucie city council members unanimously approved both the funding and operating agreements. The city said the stadium is an $80 million economic investment, and no taxpayer money will be used for its construction.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie ranks No. 67 most stressed city in U.S., 42nd for financial stress
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie was ranked as the No. 67 most stressed city in the United States according to a new WalletHub study released this month.
cards.body:
The study compared 182 cities across 39 metrics, which included average weekly work hours, unemployment rate, divorce and suicide rates. The report cited that Port St. Lucie is the 42nd most financially stressed city in America.

Jacksonville is the most stressed city in Florida, ranking No. 37 in the United States. Miami was on the list at No. 50, with affordable housing being fourth worst in the United States, and Fort Lauderdale at No. 83. WalletHub analyst Chip Lupo said cities with high crime rates, weak economies, less effective public health and congested transportation systems naturally lead to elevated stress levels for residents.

Detroit, Baltimore, Cleveland, Memphis and Shreveport, Louisiana topped the list of most stressed cities in the United States. Fremont, California, in the Bay Area, topped the list of least stressed cities, followed by South Burlington, Vermont, and Bismarck and Fargo, North Dakota.

hero.headline: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse offers 165 years of history with ocean views from 105-step climb
hero.teaser: The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, built in 1860, has guided ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years and offers panoramic views from its 105-step spiral staircase.
hero.body:
The striking red brick tower rises high above the inlet. Built in 1860, the lighthouse has guided ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years. The 105-step climb leads up a narrow spiral staircase to the gallery, which offers breathtaking panoramic views. The Atlantic Ocean stretches to the east, while the turquoise waters of the Jupiter Inlet meet the Loxahatchee and Indian rivers below. Boats glide through the channel.

The museum grounds feature restored historic buildings that tell the story of the lighthouse's past, from its construction before the Civil War to its years as an active Coast Guard station. Lighthouse keepers climbed the same stairs night after night to keep the powerful Fresnel lens shining for mariners.

hero.headline: Karolina Muchova Ends Coco Gauff's Wimbledon Run in Dramatic Tiebreaker
hero.teaser: Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker.
hero.body:
Muchova became the fourth Czech woman in the last six years to reach the final of the grass-court Grand Slam. It will be the ninth-ranked Muchova's second Grand Slam final after losing to Iga Swiatek in the 2023 French Open championship match. Muchova could face another Czech player in Saturday's final, with Linda Noskova to play Marta Kostyuk of Ukraine in the other semifinal next on Centre Court. The other Czech women in the Wimbledon final recently were Karolina Pliskova, runner-up in 2021, Marketa Vondrousova, champion in 2023, and Barbora Krejcikova, champion in 2024.

For Gauff, it was still her most successful Wimbledon. Previously, the seventh-ranked American had gone only as far as the fourth round three times, including during her breakthrough run as a 15-year-old in 2019. The men's semifinals on Friday feature top-ranked and defending champion Jannik Sinner against seven-time Wimbledon winner Novak Djokovic and French Open champion Alexander Zverev against British wild card Arthur Fery.

cards.headline: Czech Player Linda Noskova Wins Wimbledon After Blowing Five Match Points
cards.teaser: Linda Noskova recovered from a second-set meltdown in which she wasted five match points to win Wimbledon on Saturday, defeating Karolina Muchova in an all-Czech final.
cards.body:
The 21-year-old Noskova overcame Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech final on Saturday for her first Grand Slam trophy. Noskova became the third Czech woman in four years to win the grass-court major, after Marketa Vondrousova in 2023 and Barbora Krejcikova in 2024.

Petra Kvitova, who won Wimbledon in 2011 and 2014, was in attendance, as was Martina Navratilova, who won a record nine singles titles at the All England Club. Navratilova looked on from the Royal Box, where she was seated next to Kate, the Princess of Wales, who was due to present the Venus Rosewater Dish trophy to Noskova.

Muchova and Noskova played doubles together at the 2024 Paris Olympics and finished fourth. In the men's final on Sunday, top-ranked Jannik Sinner will attempt to defend his title against French Open champion Alexander Zverev.

cards.headline: Justin Bieber, Madonna to Join World Cup Final Halftime Show
cards.teaser: Justin Bieber will join Madonna, Shakira and BTS in a star-studded, Super Bowl-style halftime show at the World Cup final, FIFA announced Wednesday.
cards.body:
Justin Bieber will join fellow headliners Madonna, Shakira and BTS at the World Cup's halftime show, FIFA announced Wednesday. Afrobeats star Burna Boy, Venezuelan conductor Gustavo Dudamel and the PS22 Chorus, a choir of elementary school students based in Staten Island, New York, will also perform, the last joined by Coldplay. The 11-minute halftime performance, curated by Coldplay's Chris Martin, will take place during the final outside New York on July 19. The show will support the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund, which is raising $100 million to help children access education and soccer.

Burna Boy is one-half of this year's official song for the World Cup, "Dai Dai," led by Shakira. The song is a mesh of Afrobeats and Latin rhythms, an undeniably global, multilingual pop track. In one verse, they name a number of the world's most famous soccer players and countries competing in this year's World Cup: "Brazil, Uruguay, Argentina, Colombia," Shakira cheers. "Mexico, Japan, Korea, Netherlands." This year's World Cup halftime performance will also feature some characters from "Sesame Street," as well as Muppets like Kermit and Miss Piggy. While the Super Bowl is famed for its halftime show, such performances are not commonplace in soccer, with events like the Champions League final featuring a pre-match concert.

cards.headline: Park Vista High School Football Team Eyes State Playoffs After Strong 2025 Finish
cards.body:
Park Vista Community High School's football team is building on late-season momentum as the Cobras set their sights on the state playoffs in 2026. The Cobras struggled to find their footing early in 2025, but finished strong, winning four of their last five games. "Felt good throughout the second half of that season," senior Harris Bender said. "We're just working towards being able to carry that through the whole season, like you said, and we have all the pieces in place now, it's just about executing."

The ultimate goal is the state playoffs and eventually a state title, something the program has not achieved since 2017. Park Vista head football coach Donald Hanna stressed the importance of focus on each opponent. "We got to take it one game at a time," Hanna said. "We can't look past anyone. We got to handle business weekly and if we do that, do our job, that'll get us in the playoffs." Senior Erik Lee said, "Coming in, I feel like we got the guys that we need to get it done. But also, we got to put the work in to get there as well." Senior Justice Jones added, "It's going to feel amazing, because I already know it's gonna happen, definitely." Park Vista opens the 2026 season on the road against Atlantic in August.

hero.headline: Aldi opens in Hobe Sound as Treasure Coast shoppers seek relief from rising grocery costs
hero.teaser: A new Aldi grocery store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, bringing more affordable choices to customers already facing tight budgets. The opening comes
hero.body:
A new Aldi grocery store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, bringing more affordable choices to customers already facing tight budgets. The opening comes as the USDA expects grocery prices to rise 2.8% this year, prompting more households to adjust their purchasing decisions based on price rather than preference. For shoppers looking to stretch their dollars, the discount grocer offers an alternative to traditional supermarkets at a time when food costs continue to climb.

Customers Cheryl and Tony Cooperman said they are excited an affordable option like the new Aldi store is now open close to their home. Cheryl said grocery prices are getting expensive and are starting to change the way she shops. "They're the type of people who never used to look at prices, but now she will go with what's on sale instead of just with what they want, and they never used to do that," she said. The changing shopping habits reflect a broader trend as more households look for ways to manage rising food costs.

Price movements in key grocery categories show a mixed picture for consumers. Egg prices are dropping, and beef prices fell 1.3% from April to May, though wholesale beef prices remain at all-time highs for this time of year. Pork rose 1% from April to May, and chicken prices rose 1.3% over the same period. Fruits and vegetables are seeing an increase of less than 1%. Despite some declining categories, the overall trajectory points to continued upward pressure on grocery bills.

Shoppers James and Harry said Thursday they do not expect relief at the register anytime soon. "Prices are gonna stay inflated and are not gonna go down," they said, adding they would be willing to bet on that. Still, they said stores like Aldi, which often have lower prices than other stores, can make a difference for everyday shoppers. "Having stuff like this for the average person is extremely beneficial because there's nobody who isn't feeling the price increase," they said. The new location gives Treasure Coast residents another option for managing household budgets as inflation continues to impact the cost of food.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie teen to serve as flag bearer at FIFA World Cup finals
hero.teaser: Enrique Rosario Liz, a Port St. Lucie teenager named Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America, was surprised Friday at the Boys & Girls Club
hero.body:
Enrique Rosario Liz, a Port St. Lucie teenager named Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America, was surprised Friday at the Boys & Girls Club of St. Lucie County in Fort Pierce with a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. He will serve as one of 12 club members from across the country selected to be an official Coca-Cola flag bearer at the FIFA World Cup finals on July 19. The surprise came courtesy of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America and their partnership with the Coca-Cola Company. When the box containing the news was walked into the room surrounded by fellow club members, Rosario Liz's reaction was immediate. "I mean, this is so insane," Rosario Liz said. Along with the trip, he also received official gear inside the box.

Rosario Liz had already been juggling a packed summer, preparing for move-in at the University of Florida and an internship, but said the World Cup had been on his mind. "My time is really being taken up by the World Cup right now, forcing my parents to watch every game," Rosario Liz said. He credited the Boys & Girls Club with shaping who he has become as a leader. "The club really helped me to find what my leadership style was going to be, and really redefined what my definition of leadership was," Rosario Liz said.

The recognition as a flag bearer comes after his selection as Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region, one of the highest honors given by the Boys & Girls Clubs of America. As one of only 12 club members chosen nationally for this role, Rosario Liz will represent not only his local club in St. Lucie County but also youth organizations across the country at the World Cup finals. "The Boys & Girls Clubs has been my everything," he said.

He closed with a message for younger members at the club. "Please stay with your Boys & Girls Clubs, because one day I want to see each and every one of you in the same position that I am in right now," Rosario Liz said. The announcement marks a significant milestone for the Port St. Lucie teen as he prepares to transition to college life at the University of Florida while taking on this prestigious international role at the World Cup finals.
